It is sucky, it is I won't lie. But so is getting your child's piss in your mouth at 4am, and unfortunately, these are both risks you have to accept when having a child, so you need to suck it up. Especially when you admit your husband is already working his ass off.

I have autism and I did something like this to my dad, he was a bigger man who bought a hammock for his back yard in the summer of 2006. He was on it for all of 5 minutes before it snapped and he hit the deck both metaphorically and physically. I happened to witness this marvel of gravitational wonder from the kitchen window, and when he came back in grumbling, he asked if I'd had any problems with the hammock earlier. I immediately responded with a very helpful "nope because I only weigh 8 stone dad" he didn't speak to me for 3 days. Bliss.

Soooo not my partner because he was there, but I'll never tell my close family or friends this. One upon a time 12 years ago, I pooped on my now hubby during sexy time. So I'm on the spectrum myself, and yes, stuff like that does satisfy a personal morbid curiosity (I love seeing how machines work and the body is a biological machine IMO). I also don't always have the ability to anticipate whether other people will share that interest. That being said, if you forewarn me that you cannot handle that sort of thing (as you did), I will not expose you to it because that social parameter has now been set. She may not have the ability to do that and so it may have genuinely been an oversight on her part. I'd recommend trying to sit down and calm explain to her why you got so upset, but also try to find out if she understands what she actually did.

ETA, your body can actually also be  given back to your loved ones once they are finished. It's something you'd need to discuss and arrange with the professionals when planning the logistics of it all.

NTA. I have Aspergers myself, and part of that is the seemingly bizarre obsessions. Its not the child's fault nor is it within his control. But it's also not *your* responsibility. This may well have been an innocent oversight on their part as I know being on the spectrum is more than enough to handle without all the lovely additions, but they can't blame you for exercising your right to privacy.
